description: TIMESTRETCH mode of the trough-based grain engine: 'the time expansion is happening in the troughs' - each grain plays untouched at natural speed and SILENCE is inserted (or overlap applied, tstretch < 1) between grains so the whole stretches by tstretch. No pitch or formant change whatsoever, because no sample is resampled. Trough segmentation as grev mode 1 (wsiz-ms envelope window, trof trough depth). Verified on a 4-syllable 2.0 s file: tstretch 2.0 -> 3.0000 s with doubled gaps, 0.5 -> 0.7500 s, 3.0 -> 4.5001 s - the output is exactly troughspan x tstretch, so the model indur * tstretch OVER-predicts by the (head + tail) fraction outside the first/last troughs (-25% observed on that fixture: 3.0 actual vs 4.0 predicted; error shrinks as the grain span approaches the file length). tstretch is breakpoint-capable (verified: a 1->3 ramp renders 2.3251 s, differing from both scalar endpoints); wsiz/trof refuse breakpoints; gpcnt is accepted but INERT in this mode (gpcnt 1 and 3 byte-identical - the stretch loop advances one trough at a time regardless, source-consistent). Deterministic; MONO only.
musical_use: Time-stretching for attack-critical material: because grains are never resampled, transients stay razor-sharp while the phrase slows - speech becomes spaced-out dictation, a run of notes becomes a sequence of intact events with air between them (the manual: syllables 'more spaced out in time', not repeated). Compare psow stretch (gaps stretched pitch-synchronously, vocal-smooth) and modify speed (everything resampled, pitch shifts). tstretch < 1 compresses by overlapping the grains - a legato-izer for detached playing. Breakpoint tstretch for phrasing: 1.0 rising to 3.0 makes an accelerando-in-reverse (progressive spacing) within one pass. Rule of thumb for segmentation: wsiz ~ feature-length/3 (enforced ceiling indur/3), trof ~0.4-0.5.

wsiz.description: Envelope window in ms (feature size / 3 rule). CDP-enforced, input-dependent ceiling indur/3: '(0.181406 to 666.666667)' on a 2 s file. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 ... brkpnt_files not permitted').

trof.description: Acceptable trough height relative to adjacent peaks. Refusal quotes '(0.000002 to 0.999998)' yet exact 0 and 1.0 are accepted (probed) - stay inside (0,1). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 2 ... brkpnt_files not permitted').

gpcnt.description: Grains per unit - required by the argv but INERT in this mode: gpcnt 1 and 3 render byte-identical (the TSTRETCH loop advances trough-by-trough regardless; the banner's 'GPCNT ... can vary over time' does not apply here). Set it to 1.

tstretch.description: Stretch ratio for the whole output; grains themselves are NOT stretched (CDP-enforced 'Parameter[4] Value (200.000000) out of range (0.010000 to 100.000000)' / same for 0.005). Breakpoint-CAPABLE (banner-confirmed; verified: a 1.0->3.0 ramp renders 2.3251 s, differing from the x1 (1.5000 s) and x3 (4.5001 s) scalar renders).

examples.description: Double-space a spoken phrase without touching its pitch.
examples.expected_use: Syllables intact, gaps doubled; expect ~trough-span x 2, a little under indur x 2.

examples.description: Progressive spacing: stretch grows 1x to 3x across the file.
examples.expected_use: Phrase starts at natural pace and pulls apart (write str_ramp.brk with breakpoint(): 0.0 1.0 / end 3.0).

known_issues: Duration honesty: actual = (trough span) x tstretch - the head before the first trough and tail after the last are DISCARDED, so indur * tstretch over-predicts by that fraction (observed -25% on a 4-syllable fixture whose troughs span 1.5 s of 2.0 s; -20% at x0.5). The model is the upper bound; the shortfall is material-dependent, small on densely-evented sources.
gpcnt is required but inert in this mode (byte-identical outputs for 1 vs 3) - a divergence from the banner's 'GPCNT ... can vary over time' claim, which holds for modes 1-4 but not 5.
Refusals: pure tone 'ERROR: NO PEAKS IN THE FILE'; flat noise 'ERROR: INSUFFICIENT VALID TROUGHS IN THE FILE.'; stereo 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' (MONO only).
trof accepts the out-of-range endpoints 0 and 1.0 despite refusing 1.5 with '(0.000002 to 0.999998)'.
tstretch < 1 overlaps grains rather than cutting them - levels can sum; watch for clipping on dense material.
